definitions.explanation: A printing method using raised metal or wooden type pieces that are inked and pressed onto paper, or the type pieces themselves.

examples.english: Letterpress printing became widespread in Japan during the Meiji era, and today it is being reevaluated as a hobby and art form.

notes:
A compound of {活|かつ} (movable/living) and {版|ぱん} (printing plate/block). The word is short for {活字版|かつじばん} (movable type printing plate). This technology was revolutionary for mass-producing printed text.

Although largely replaced by offset printing and digital methods for commercial use, letterpress has experienced a revival as a craft. Workshops offering {活版|かっぱん}⟦{印刷|いんさつ}→印刷：01844_insatsu⟧ experiences are popular in Japan, and many stationery enthusiasts seek out letterpress-printed postcards and business cards for their tactile quality — the slight indentation left by the type on paper.
